Alpine's postgresql16 16.15-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 16.15 and lists CVE-2026-14678 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 16 release. The pg_trgm module is present: pg_trgm.so ships in the postgresql16-contrib package of every published build for Alpine 3.23, on both x86_64 and aarch64. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases, their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine's secfixes do not list this CVE for them, so they are recorded as affected; 16.15-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-14678 (PostgreSQL pg_trgm picksplit reads past end of buffer): a buffer over-read in the pg_trgm GiST index picksplit function, which might let a table maintainer infer limited memory values from index split choices. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14678/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_17_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/1af08af694815520e5642dc3a85cc010cbcf9f84 (Security: CVE-2026-14678, in tag REL_17_11 and not in REL_17_10), which changes only gtrgm_picksplit() in contrib/pg_trgm/trgm_gist.c, so that, when one side of a split is all-true and the entry being placed is not, it passes the entry's cached signature bit vector to sizebitvec() directly instead of through the GETSIGN() macro, which expects an index value with a header, skips that header and so reads past the end of the bit vector's buffer. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14678 under 17.11-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD on that branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the current 17.12-r0 build uses the APKBUILD at that commit, and none of its patches changes the file the fix changes, nor do the patches of the 17.11-r0 APKBUILD on that branch. The pg_trgm module, /usr/lib/postgresql17/pg_trgm.so, ships in the postgresql17-contrib package of every published build for Alpine 3.23 on both architectures. We read every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64, checking each against the repository index checksum: /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres in each reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0 are built from PostgreSQL releases before 17.11 and are affected; 17.11-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-14678 (PostgreSQL pg_trgm picksplit reads past end of buffer) affects PostgreSQL 18 before 18.6 and is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14678/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list it. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/849019a50a0ccbc7a7fe2ab3db53078ec2f99131 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-14678, which is in the REL_18_6 release tag and not in REL_18_4; it changes only contrib/pg_trgm/trgm_gist.c, so that the GiST picksplit function no longer reads a cached signature as a trigram array. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes say so), so although Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14678 under an 18.5-r0 secfixes entry, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64, and we checked every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index. The vulnerable module, /usr/lib/postgresql18/pg_trgm.so, ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of every one of those builds on both architectures. In each build the version strings of the postgres server binary and of the client programs (psql, pg_dump, pg_dumpall, pg_restore, pg_basebackup and pg_config) report the PostgreSQL release that matches the package version (18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4, 18.6 and 18.7 respectively). The fix adds no message text that marks it in the binaries, so the boundary rests on the release each build reports. 18.6-r0 is the first published build carrying the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before 18.6 and are affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14678, a buffer over-read in the pg_trgm index picksplit function, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14678/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14678. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
